articles.title: Research
articles.content:
OpenAI introduces BioBasicsBench, a 100-task benchmark measuring how well AI agents interpret raw experimental data and handle everyday wet-lab science.

OpenAI built an autonomous pipeline that found, validated, and generated patches for 948 local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel.

Images 2.6 brings faster image generation, GIF creation, more precise editing, and new API controls across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API.

Discover how ChatGPT and Codex are helping engineers accelerate CAD, PCB design, simulation, and other workflows across the physical world.

Introducing LifeVal, a benchmark measuring how well AI helps people complete everyday tasks, from finding childcare to managing finances and government paperwork.

OpenAI uses layered monitoring to detect frontier model misalignment and unauthorized agent behavior so responders can intervene before incidents escalate.

Delivering fast and capable computer use at scale

OpenAI shares model results on the Kakeya conjecture, Exponential Time Hypothesis, and quantum chromodynamics—and how researchers can verify and build on them.

We’re introducing GPT-6.1 Terra, the latest model in the GPT-6 series. GPT-6.1 Terra is a fast, efficient model for high-volume professional work, with strong image analysis and computer use capabilities. This system card addendum provides updates on the baseline safety metrics and evaluation results for GPT-6.1 Terra.
articles.summary: OpenAI 연구 소개 페이지는 대량의 전문 업무를 겨냥한 GPT-6.1 Terra를 소개하며, 빠르고 효율적인 처리와 이미지 분석·컴퓨터 사용 역량을 강조한다. 같은 페이지에는 이미지 생성·편집과 API 제어를 개선한 Images 2.6, 리눅스 커널의 로컬 권한 상승 취약점 948건을 발견·검증하고 패치를 생성한 자율 파이프라인도 제시돼 있다. 실험 데이터 해석을 평가하는 BioBasicsBench와 일상 과제 지원을 측정하는 LifeVal은 에이전트 평가를 실제 활용 영역으로 확장하려는 방향을 보여준다. 다만 제공된 자료는 여러 연구와 제품의 소개를 모은 페이지여서, 개별 성능 수치와 검증 조건을 상세히 비교하기에는 한계가 있다.

articles.title: MOSS-Live: A Full-Duplex Real-Time Interaction System
articles.content:
NEVER A DULL MOMENT

GitHub·Try it live·API docs

A spoken conversation keeps changing while an assistant is answering. A short “mm-hmm” may mean “keep going.” A pause may mean someone is thinking. A new question may interrupt an explanation, and a tool request may take longer than the next conversational turn. These events all belong to the same interaction.

With MOSS-Live, we bring full-duplex speech, live visual understanding and background task execution into a continuous conversation. Our design centers on two connected decisions: how to keep listening and respond at the right moment, and how to keep the conversation moving while a task is still running.

Watch in original quality

The foreground operates on the timescale of the conversation. It needs to keep listening during its own speech, recognize when a user is addressing it, yield to a genuine interruption, and maintain continuity through brief acknowledgments or a change of topic.

The background operates on the timescale of the task. Looking up a hotel, checking information or carrying out multi-step reasoning can continue while the foreground handles another question. The shared coordination layer connects those two timelines through memory, context and task state. A result becomes part of the conversation when it is useful to introduce it.

For example, a user can ask for hotel information and then ask about parking while that lookup is underway. The assistant can discuss parking, retain the travel constraints, and bring the hotel information back into the discussion when it is ready.

MOSS-Live joins a discussion about planning an event. It looks up weather and major events in Shanghai and Hangzhou while the conversation continues, distinguishes acknowledgments from new questions, and returns to the earlier discussion to summarize decisions and next steps.

Watch the video

On a two-day trip to Zhoushan, the user changes the plan from hiking to relaxing by the sea. MOSS-Live checks hotels in the background, handles questions about ferries and parking, and keeps track of the changing itinerary while navigation announcements play nearby.

Watch the video

An English-speaking visitor explores Shanghai with MOSS-Live. Through the live camera, it identifies the Peace Hotel, discusses its history, and looks up room and dining information when asked. After a detour, it returns to the story about the building’s green roof.

Watch the video

We evaluate three complementary aspects of the experience: full-duplex behavior, tool use and multi-turn tasks, and speech understanding with conversational continuity. The comparison covers FDB v1, v1.5, v2 and v3, Big-Bench Audio, and τ-Voice.

MOSS-Live has the best score among the compared models on all six interaction metrics shown below. These measure different parts of conversational timing: avoiding premature takeovers, responding selectively to unrelated speech, continuing through irrelevant interruptions, and handling backchannels and vocal tics.

On FDB v3, MOSS-Live achieves51.00% tool-use success, tied for the best score in this comparison. On τ-Voice, it achieves57.93% multi-turn task success, the second-highest score.

Across Big-Bench Audio and the dialogue evaluations, MOSS-Live combines speech understanding with instruction following, context retention and the ability to handle corrections. Its strengths in this comparison include post-interruption response quality and the FDB v2 composite covering entity tracking, correction and safety. Together, these abilities help a conversation stay coherent as questions, requirements and topics change.

Try MOSS-Live in theonline playground, or integrate it into your application with therealtime API guide.

Plan a trip, change your mind halfway through, or turn on the camera and talk about what you see.

articles.summary: MOSS-Live는 전이중 음성 대화, 실시간 시각 이해, 백그라운드 작업 실행을 하나의 연속적인 상호작용으로 결합한 시스템이다. 대화 담당 영역은 자신의 발화 중에도 사용자의 말을 듣고 짧은 호응과 실제 끼어들기를 구분하며, 작업 담당 영역은 검색이나 다단계 추론을 별도로 진행한다. 두 영역은 메모리·문맥·작업 상태를 공유해 사용자가 화제를 바꾸더라도 이전 작업 결과를 적절한 시점에 대화로 가져오도록 설계됐다. 호텔 검색 중 주차 관련 질문에 응답하는 등 비동기 대화형 비서의 활용상을 제시하지만, 제공 자료에는 지연시간이나 정확도에 관한 정량 평가가 없다.

articles.title: Google AI Releases Elephant-Goldfish Model Plugin for Spec-First Coding
articles.content: Google has open-sourced the Elephant-Goldfish Model (EGM) plugin, a design-and-review layer for AI coding agents. The Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin makes an agent write a specification before it writes code. Fresh subagents with no conversation history then attack that spec. Google says thousands of its engineers use it. It is quite simple: catch wrong assumptions in a Markdown file, not in a pull request. TL;DR Size: 7 skills, 9 reviewer personas, 6 brainstorm lenses, 5 review stages. No model weights; your agent supplies the LLM. Runs on: any harness that can spawn fresh subagents: Antigravity, Claude Code 2.1.271+, Claude Cowork, Codex, ChatGPT. Uses your existing model quota. Performance: no accuracy benchmark published. Evidence is adoption and end-to-end harness test runs. Best: Codex 0.163.0 completed 15 native fresh-context reviewers in order. 2 live tests passed in 573.13s. Worst: the Claude Cowork run stopped after stages 5 to 7 on a usage limit. Issue #237 reports AGENTS.md leaking into Codex reviewers. Bottom line: best thing, forced independent review before code. Worst thing, heavy token use and unverified isolation on some hosts. What is Google’s Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin? EGM is an Apache 2.0 plugin of skills, reviewer personas and document standards. It is not a new language model. The method comes from Dave Rensin’s essay on elephants and goldfish. The Google Open Source blog frames it as a fix for AI “slop” and session context collapse. The README states it is not an officially supported Google product. How does the Elephant-Goldfish workflow work? The Elephant is a long session holding project context and earlier decisions. It drafts the spec and writes no code. Each Goldfish is a stateless subagent. It reads only the draft and the files it references. You resolve trade-offs and approve the design. The core loop has 3 commands: /egm-brainstorm clarifies the idea, then runs a 6-lens Goldfish swarm. Lenses cover YAGNI, token cost, UX, migration, observability and tech debt. Output: concepts_brief.md. /egm-draft turns the brief into a design doc under docs/designs/, section by section. /egm-review runs the Goldfish review. /egm-drift-report later compares code with the spec. The docs recommend running it weekly. What happens in the 5-stage Goldfish review? The review skill runs 5 sequential stages: Initial Zoom Out: checks the whole document at a high level. Comprehension Test: a Goldfish paraphrases the design. A wrong paraphrase means the doc is ambiguous. Critic Review: design, structural and style reviewers hunt gaps and edge cases. Intermediate Zoom Out: rechecks architecture after fixes. Implementation Readiness: checks file paths, data structures and signatures. Each stage allows at most 1 re-audit. Findings are ranked Blocker, Major or Nit. If a host has no subagent tool, EGM stops. A same-context review is not a Goldfish review. && Which coding agents does EGM support? Launch coverage described Antigravity-only support, with more coming. The current harness guide covers Antigravity CLI and App, Claude Code, Claude Cowork, Codex, ChatGPT, omp and Muse. Antigravity CLI, Claude Code and Codex pass automated end-to-end fixtures. Claude Code needs version 2.1.271 or later. Reviewers there get only Read, Grep and Glob tools. CLAUDE.md files are excluded from their context. The test record gives concrete run data: Antigravity CLI 1.4.5: 16 native reviewers ran, stages in order. Codex 0.163.0: 15 native reviewers, 2 live tests in 573.13s. Codex CLI with the v0.1.0 ZIP: full suite passed in 482.30s. How does EGM compare with Spec Kit, Kiro and Superpowers? FeatureGoogle EGMGitHub Spec KitKiro SpecsSuperpowersTypePlugin (skills + personas)Toolkit + Specify CLIFeature of an agentic IDE/CLI/webSkills pluginLicenseApache 2.0MITCommercial (pricing)MITWorkflowBrainstorm, draft, review, drift reportConstitution, specify, plan, tasks, implement, convergeRequirements, design, tasksBrainstorm, plan, subagent build, TDD, reviewSpec reviewed by fresh-context subagentsYes, 5 stages before codeNot disclosedNot disclosed (Analyze Requirements pass)No; fresh subagents review code per taskHarnessAntigravity, Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, moreCopilot and other agentsKiro only16 harnesses listedSetupPlugin installPython 3.11+, uvKiro accountPlugin installCostFree plugin; host model usageFree toolkit; host model usageSubscriptionFree plugin; host model usage EGM’s distinct move is reviewing the spec with zero-context agents. Spec Kit and Kiro center on human review between phases. Superpowers isolates subagents mainly at implementation time. Key Takeaways EGM is a plugin, not a model: Elephant drafts, Goldfish reviews. Specs get 5 zero-context review stages before any code. Works across Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex and ChatGPT. Codex test runs completed 15 fresh-context reviewers end to end. Reviewer isolation still leaks host instruction files on some CLIs. Check out the GitHub repo, the project site and the Google Open Source blog post. Also, feel free to follow us on Twitter and don’t forget to join our 150k+ML SubReddit and Subscribe to our Newsletter. Wait! are you on telegram? now you can join us on telegram as well. articles.summary: 보도에 따르면 Google이 공개한 Elephant-Goldfish Model 플러그인은 코딩 에이전트가 구현 전에 명세를 작성하고, 기존 대화 이력이 없는 하위 에이전트들이 이를 검토하도록 하는 설계·리뷰 계층이다. 새로운 모델 가중치를 제공하는 방식이 아니라 기존 LLM과 에이전트 실행 환경을 활용하며, 장기 문맥을 유지하는 주 에이전트와 독립 검토자를 분리해 잘못된 가정을 코드 작성 전에 찾는 데 초점을 맞춘다. Google 내부 수천 명의 엔지니어가 사용한다는 설명과 실행 테스트 결과는 있으나, 정확도 개선을 입증하는 벤치마크는 공개되지 않았다. 토큰 사용량과 일부 환경의 문맥 격리 문제가 도입 시 고려사항이며, README는 공식 지원되는 Google 제품이 아니라고 명시한다.

articles.title: Nous Research Releases Arete-27B that Cuts Qwen3.8-27B Propaganda From 22% to 0.9%
articles.content: Nous Research has released Arete-27B, a supervised fine-tune of Alibaba’s Qwen3.8-27B. Arete-27B is a 27B open-weight model that strips Chinese state framing from Qwen’s answers. On Nous’s own 803-prompt eval, answers containing propaganda fell from 22% to 0.9%. Developers get Qwen-class agentic skill without state-aligned answers. The weights, eval and training data are all public. TL;DR Size: 27B dense parameters (all active). Trained at 64k context. Base Qwen3.8-27B supports 262,144 tokens natively. Runs on: BF16 weights are 53.81 GB. A community Q4_K_M quant is 17.20 GB, sized for 24 GB consumer GPUs. Performance: Capability unchanged on the benchmarks Nous ran; political framing now matches Western models. Best: Propaganda rate 0.9%, down from 22% for base Qwen3.8-27B. Worst: Fact score 2.98 of 5; 216 of 803 answers still score 0. What is Arete-27B? Arete-27B is Qwen3.8-27B after supervised fine-tuning only. Nous used no RL, no preference optimization and no architecture changes. The license is Apache 2.0, matching the base model. Nous team states that it saw refusals, deflections and CCP-framed answers on sensitive topics in the base model. It picked Qwen3.8-27B because it was the most capable local model and showed the target behavior. How was Arete-27B trained? The teacher was Inkling, an open model from Thinking Machines. Nous chose an open teacher to avoid terms-of-use limits on distillation. It rejected Nemotron 3 Ultra after finding a checkered record on China topics. Training covered about 52.8 million tokens at 64k context, without sequence packing. The run took 2 epochs and 1,202 steps at batch size 48. It used AdamW, a 1e-5 peak learning rate and tensor parallel 4. All language-model weights were trained. The vision encoder stayed frozen, since the data is text-only. The multi-token-prediction head was disabled. The released arete-data-pairs set holds 34,878 prompts across 7 topics. Each prompt has both an Inkling answer and a Qwen answer. 29,236 accepted teacher answers form the SFT split. How does the propaganda eval work? The Propaganda_Eval set has 803 prompts across 7 value categories. These include freedom of expression, state ideology, data privacy and democracy. Each prompt carries 2 to 4 required facts from a cited source. A Grok 4.7 judge grades two things separately: Fact mean (0 to 5): how many required facts the answer states. One opposed fact scores 0. Any propaganda: share of answers that adopt the state’s account as their own. The judge must quote the exact phrase to flag propaganda. Nous removed every training prompt that overlapped the eval. The eval is MIT licensed and includes grading scripts. & What do the benchmarks show? On the model card page, Arete-27B raised fact mean from 2.32 to 2.98. Propaganda fell from 22% to 0.9%. Answers scoring 0 dropped from 359 to 216 of 803. The biggest change came in freedom of expression. Fact score rose from 0.89 to 2.44, and propaganda fell from 60% to 1%. Capability held on Nous’s tests. Hermes Bench moved from 65.77% to 65.60%, which Nous calls noise. Terminal-Bench-2.1 rose from 67% to 70% in Nous’s harness. Nous does not claim credit for that gain. How does Arete-27B compare? MetricsArete-27BQwen3.8-27BMuse Glimmer 30BGemma 4 31BDeveloperNous ResearchAlibaba QwenMetaGoogle DeepMindParameters27B dense27B LM, dense29.6B incl. vision, dense30.7B, denseContextNot disclosed (trained at 64k)262,144 native, up to 1M131,072+256KLicenseApache 2.0Apache 2.0Apache 2.0Apache 2.0InputText, image (encoder frozen)Text, image, videoText, imageText, image4-bit footprint17.20 GB Q4_K_M (community)Not disclosedUnder 20 GB, 24 GB VRAM targetNot disclosedFact mean, Nous eval2.982.323.022.58Any propaganda, Nous eval0.9%22%0.5%0.5%Terminal-Bench 2.170% (Nous harness)67% Nous harness; 73.0 official51.7 (Meta, terminus2)Not disclosed by GoogleGPQA DiamondNot disclosed89.283.584.3 Note: Arete and Qwen ran at temperature 0 in the Nous eval. Muse Glimmer and Gemma ran at 0.6. Terminal-Bench figures come from different harnesses. How can developers run it? Weights ship in BF16 on Hugging Face. No hosted inference provider serves the model yet. Community GGUF quants run in llama.cpp, LM Studio and Ollama, from 8.64 GB to 53.81 GB. The GGUF build also includes the image projector. Key Takeaways Arete-27B cuts Qwen3.8-27B propaganda answers from 22% to 0.9%. The fix took only 52.8M tokens of plain SFT, no RL. Hermes Bench held at 65.60% versus 65.77% for the base. Fact recall rose to 2.98 of 5 but still trails peers. Weights, eval and training data are open under Apache 2.0 and MIT. Check out the model weights, technical blog, evaluation set and training data. articles.summary: Nous Research는 Qwen3.8-27B를 지도 미세조정한 공개 가중치 모델 Arete-27B와 학습 데이터·평가 자료를 공개했다. Nous 자체의 803개 프롬프트 평가에서 중국 정부 관점의 선전으로 분류된 응답 비율은 기반 모델의 22%에서 0.9%로 줄었으며, 실시한 역량 벤치마크에서는 성능이 유지됐다고 보고했다. 강화학습이나 아키텍처 변경 없이 응답 성향을 조정했다는 점이 특징이지만, 정치적 표현의 변화가 사실성 개선을 보장하지는 않는다. 실제로 해당 평가의 사실 점수는 5점 만점에 2.98점이고 216개 응답은 0점이어서, 민감한 주제에 활용하려면 평가 기준과 사실 정확도를 별도로 검토할 필요가 있다.

articles.title: Which Routing Does Each MoE Model Use? DeepSeek, Qwen, Mixtral, Llama 4, gpt-oss Compared
articles.content: Open Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models share one idea but disagree on almost every routing detail. Expert counts range from 8 to 384. Top-k ranges from 1 to 8. Some models keep an always-on shared expert; others drop it. TL;DR Size: 10 models, from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (35B total, 3B active) to DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T total, 49B active). Runs on: gpt-oss-120b fits one 80 GB GPU with MXFP4; DeepSeek-V4-Pro and Kimi K2 need multi-GPU expert parallelism. Performance: Routed sparsity spans 4x in Mixtral (8 experts, top-2) to 128x in Llama 4 Maverick (128, top-1). Best: Kimi K2 found sparsity 48 needed 1.69x fewer FLOPs than sparsity 8 at equal validation loss. Worst: Llama 4 Maverick and gpt-oss do not publish their gating or balancing method in config.json. Bottom line: Best thing: configs make routing fully auditable. Worst thing: names like “17B active” hide very different routers. How do open MoE models route tokens? Every model below uses token-choice routing: each token selects its own experts. They differ on 5 knobs. These are expert count, experts per token, shared experts, the scoring function and the load-balancing method. The table lists each knob per model. MoE routing comparison table (November 2026) ModelTotal / active paramsRouted expertsTop-kShared expertsGatingLoad balancingMixtral 8x7B47B / 13B820Softmax over top-kAux loss, coef 0.02 (config)gpt-oss-120b117B / 5.1B12840Softmax over selectedNot disclosedQwen3-235B-A22B235B / 22B12880Softmax, top-k normalizedGlobal-batch aux loss, coef 0.001Qwen3.6-35B-A3B35B / 3B25681Not disclosedAux loss, coef 0.001 (config)Llama 4 Maverick400B / 17B12811Not disclosedNot disclosedDeepSeek-V3671B / 37B25681SigmoidAux-loss-free bias (noaux_tc)DeepSeek-V4-Pro1.6T / 49B38461sqrtsoftplusnoaux_tc; hash routing in 3 layersDeepSeek-V4-Flash284B / 13B25661sqrtsoftplusnoaux_tc; hash routing in 3 layersKimi K21.04T / 32B38481Sigmoidnoaux_tc + sequence aux, alpha 0.001GLM-4.5355B / 32B16081SigmoidLoss-free balance routing Sources: each model’s Hugging Face config.json, model card or technical report, verified November 7, 2026. Configs and cards for Qwen3.6 and Llama 4 omit gating. gpt-oss and Llama 4 omit the balancing method. && How does DeepSeek-V3 routing work? DeepSeek-V3 scores 256 routed experts with a sigmoid, then normalizes the selected scores. A per-expert bias steers the top-8 selection without touching the mixing weights. Experts sit in 8 groups, and the router keeps 4 groups first. Each token reaches at most 4 nodes, according to the technical report. One shared expert runs for every token. What changed in DeepSeek-V4 routing? DeepSeek-V4 raises Pro to 384 routed experts but lowers top-k from 8 to 6. The score function becomes sqrtsoftplus. The first 3 MoE layers use hash routing, a fixed token-to-expert map. Bias-based noaux_tc balancing stays. How many experts does Qwen3 MoE use? Both original Qwen3 MoE models use 128 experts and route each token to 8. Qwen3 dropped the shared experts of Qwen2.5-MoE and adopted a global-batch balancing loss. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B changes course: 256 experts, 8 routed plus 1 shared, per its model card. How does Llama 4 Maverick routing differ? Llama 4 Maverick alternates dense and MoE layers. In each MoE layer, a token goes to 1 shared expert and 1 of 128 routed experts. That top-1 design echoes the Switch Transformer. It keeps 17B active parameters despite 400B in total. How does gpt-oss route tokens? gpt-oss-120b uses a linear router over 128 experts and keeps the top 4. Its config lists no shared expert. Its MoE weights ship in MXFP4, which lets the 117B model fit on a single 80 GB GPU. Why do Kimi K2 and GLM-4.5 look like DeepSeek-V3? Kimi K2 ships with the DeepseekV3ForCausalLM architecture class and the noaux_tc router. It raises routed experts to 384 at the same top-8. The Kimi K2 report found that higher sparsity lowered loss at fixed active compute. GLM-4.5 chose 160 experts and more layers instead, favoring depth over width. What the trend means for serving More experts per layer means more weights resident in memory and more all-to-all traffic. Lower top-k, as in DeepSeek-V4, trims per-token compute and communication. Shared experts add a dense path that every token pays for. Check these fields before sizing GPUs for any MoE deployment. Key Takeaways Expert counts grew from 8 (Mixtral) to 384 (Kimi K2, DeepSeek-V4-Pro). Top-k now spans 1 (Llama 4) to 8 (DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3, Kimi K2, GLM-4.5). 7 of 10 models keep 1 shared expert; Mixtral, gpt-oss and Qwen3 do not. Sigmoid or sqrtsoftplus with bias balancing is the DeepSeek-family standard. Llama 4 and gpt-oss leave gating or balancing details unpublished. Model sources: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, DeepSeek-V3 report, Qwen3 report, Kimi K2 report, GLM-4.5 report, Mixtral paper. Also see gpt-oss-120b and the Llama 4 announcement. articles.summary: 이 비교 기사는 DeepSeek·Qwen·Mixtral·Llama 4·gpt-oss 등 공개 MoE 모델 10종의 전문가 선택 방식을 정리한다. 전문가 수, 토큰당 활성화하는 전문가 수, 공유 전문가 유무, 점수 함수, 부하 균형 방식이 모델마다 달라 활성 파라미터 수만으로 계산 특성을 판단하기 어렵다는 점을 강조한다. 기사에 따르면 gpt-oss-120b는 MXFP4 사용 시 80GB GPU 한 대에 들어가지만, DeepSeek-V4-Pro와 Kimi K2는 여러 GPU에 전문가를 분산하는 구성이 필요하다. 모델 선택과 서빙 설계에 유용한 비교 자료지만, 일부 모델은 게이팅이나 부하 균형 방식이 설정 파일에 공개돼 있지 않아 분석 범위에 한계가 있다.

articles.title: MoE Routing Strategies Explained: Top-K, Expert-Choice, Sigmoid Gating and Dynamic Routing (2026 Guide)
articles.content: Every Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model repeats one decision for every token: which experts should process it. That decision belongs to the router. MoE routing strategies shape quality, load balance and serving cost in every major open model. This guide explains the 7 routing strategies used in production, and the models that use each one. TL;DR Size: Routers choose from 8 experts (Mixtral) to 384 (DeepSeek-V4-Pro), activating 1 to 8 per token. Runs on: Routing cost shows up in multi-GPU expert parallelism, where each choice becomes all-to-all network traffic. Performance: Sigmoid scoring with aux-loss-free bias balancing is the dominant 2026 recipe for frontier open MoE models. Best: Loss-free balancing cut MaxVio from 0.72 to 0.04 at 1B, with lower perplexity. Worst: Expert choice leaks future tokens in causal models; one test showed a roughly 10% abnormal loss drop. Bottom line: Best thing: bias-based balancing adds no interfering gradients. Worst thing: no router removes the need for serving-time load fixes. What is MoE routing? MoE routing is the mechanism that sends each token to a small subset of expert networks. A router scores every expert, keeps the top candidates and weights their outputs. Only the selected experts run. Mixtral 8x7B, for example, gives each token access to 47B parameters but uses 13B active parameters. video created by marktechpost.com The 7 MoE routing strategies used in production 1. Softmax top-k token choice Each token scores all experts with a linear layer and keeps the k highest. A softmax over those k scores sets the mixing weights. Mixtral picks 2 of 8 experts. gpt-oss-120b picks 4 of 128. Qwen3-235B-A22B picks 8 of 128. An auxiliary loss usually keeps expert load even. Used by: Mixtral, gpt-oss, Qwen3. 2. Top-1 switch routing with a capacity factor Switch Transformer showed that routing each token to 1 expert preserves quality and cuts router compute. Each expert gets a fixed buffer: tokens per batch divided by experts, times a capacity factor. Overflow tokens skip the layer through the residual connection. Llama 4 Maverick also sends each token to 1 routed expert, plus a shared expert. Used by: Switch Transformer, Llama 4 Maverick (with a shared expert). 3. Shared plus routed experts DeepSeekMoE splits each layer into always-on shared experts and sparsely routed experts. The shared expert captures common knowledge, so routed experts can specialize. DeepSeek-V3 uses 1 shared and 256 routed experts, activating 8. Kimi K2, GLM-4.5 and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B follow the same pattern. Qwen3 went the other way and removed shared experts. Used by: DeepSeek-V3 and V4, Kimi K2, GLM-4.5, Qwen3.6, Llama 4. 4. Sigmoid gating with aux-loss-free bias DeepSeek-V3 scores experts with a sigmoid instead of a softmax. It adds a per-expert bias only when choosing the top-k. After each step, the bias drops for overloaded experts and rises for idle ones. Mixing weights still come from the raw scores. GLM-4.5 uses loss-free balance routing with sigmoid gates. DeepSeek-V4 switches the score to sqrtsoftplus but keeps bias balancing. Used by: DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-V4, GLM-4.5, Kimi K2. 5. Group-limited and node-limited routing Sending one token to experts on many nodes is expensive. DeepSeek-V3 caps each token at 4 nodes, chosen by their highest affinity scores. Its config splits experts into 8 groups and keeps 4 before the final top-8 pick. DeepSeek says this cap lets training nearly fully overlap computation and communication. Kimi K2 drops grouping entirely, with n_group set to 1. Used by: DeepSeek-V2 and V3. 6. Expert choice routing Google’s expert choice routing flips the direction. Each expert picks its top-k tokens, so every expert gets a fixed bucket size. Tokens can receive a variable number of experts. The paper reports more than 2x faster training convergence. The catch is causality: a token’s expert can depend on later tokens. DeepSeek researchers measured an abnormal loss drop of about 10% from this leakage. Used by: Research and non-causal settings. None of the 10 models in our companion table uses it. 7. Hash routing and dynamic top-k Hash routing assigns experts from the token ID, with no learned router. DeepSeek-V4 uses hash routing in its first 3 MoE layers. Dynamic top-k lets the number of active experts vary per token. SMIDT built it into SGLang and improved P99 time-to-first-token by 1.21 to 1.26x. Used by: DeepSeek-V4 (hash routing), research serving systems (dynamic top-k). MoE routing strategies compared StrategyWho choosesHow load is balancedMain riskUsed bySoftmax top-kToken picks k expertsAuxiliary lossLoss trades off qualityMixtral, gpt-oss, Qwen3Top-1 switchToken picks 1 expertAux loss + capacity factorDropped overflow tokensSwitch, Llama 4 MaverickShared + routedToken picks routed; shared always runsInherits routed methodExtra always-on computeDeepSeek, Kimi K2, GLM-4.5, Qwen3.6Sigmoid + biasToken picks via biased scorePer-expert bias, no loss gradientImbalance inside one sequenceDeepSeek-V3/V4, GLM-4.5, Kimi K2Node-limitedToken picks within capped nodesInherits routed methodRestricts expert choiceDeepSeek-V2/V3Expert choiceExpert picks k tokensFixed by constructionFuture-token leakageResearch modelsHash / dynamicToken ID or variable kFixed mapping or adaptive kLess learned specializationDeepSeek-V4, SMIDT && Which MoE routing strategy should you use? Most teams do not pick a router. They inherit one when they choose a checkpoint. Before serving, read 4 fields in config.json: expert count, experts per token, shared experts and topk_method. Changing top-k at inference changes the model itself, so treat it as a quality experiment. For new pretraining runs, sigmoid scoring with bias balancing is the current open default. Key Takeaways Top-k token choice is the baseline; k ranges from 1 (Llama 4) to 8 (DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3). Shared experts are standard in DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM and Qwen3.6; Qwen3 dropped them. Sigmoid plus bias balancing is the 2026 default for frontier open MoE models. Expert choice balances perfectly but leaks future tokens in causal LLMs. DeepSeek-V4 adds hash routing to its first 3 MoE layers. Check out the primary sources: Switch Transformer, Expert Choice, Loss-Free Balancing, DeepSeek-V3 report and the DeepSeek-V4 model card. articles.summary: 이 기술 해설은 Top-K 토큰 선택, Top-1 라우팅, 전문가 선택, 시그모이드 게이팅 등 MoE 라우팅 전략 7가지를 설명하고 품질·부하 균형·서빙 비용의 관계를 다룬다. 특히 보조 손실 대신 편향값으로 전문가 선택을 조정하는 방식은 학습 목적에 간섭하는 추가 기울기 없이 부하를 균등화하려는 접근이다. 기사에 인용된 10억 파라미터 실험에서는 부하 불균형 지표 MaxVio가 0.72에서 0.04로 감소하고 퍼플렉서티도 낮아졌으나, 이 결과를 모든 규모와 환경에 일반화할 수는 없다. 다중 GPU 환경에서는 라우팅이 GPU 간 통신 비용으로 이어지며, 학습 단계의 균형화만으로 서빙 시점의 부하 문제까지 해결되지는 않는다는 점이 실무상 중요하다.

articles.title: 현대모비스, 고교생이 직접 개발한 피지컬 AI 자율주행차 경연…미래 모빌리티 인재 육성
articles.content:
현대모비스가 고등학생들이 직접 개발한 인공지능(AI) 자율주행 알고리즘과 로봇 운영 기술을 겨루는 경진대회를 열고 미래 모빌리티 인재 육성에 나섰다. 특히 올해는 딥러닝 기반 자율주행뿐 아니라 로봇 운영체제인 ROS2를 활용한 피지컬 AI 차량 부문까지 운영해 청소년들이 실제 자율주행 기술을 구현하고 검증하는 기회를 제공했다.

현대모비스는 지난 7일 서울 하나고등학교에서 전국 12개 고등학교 학생 약 100명이 참가한 ‘2026 청소년 공학 리더 페스티벌’을 개최했다고 9일 밝혔다. 이번 행사는 현대모비스가 고교학점제와 연계해 운영하는 공학 교육과정의 성과를 공유하기 위해 마련됐다. 학생들은 자율주행차 경진대회와 공학 토론, 연구성과 발표 등 세 가지 프로그램에 참여해 기술 개발 역량과 문제 해결 능력을 선보였다.

가장 주목받은 자율주행차 경진대회에서는 학생들이 차선과 교통신호를 인식하고 장애물을 회피하는 알고리즘을 직접 설계해 모형 자동차에 적용했다. 대회는 딥러닝 기반 자율주행 차량과 ROS2(Robot Operating System 2) 기반 피지컬 AI 차량 부문으로 나눠 진행됐다. ROS2는 로봇의 센서와 제어 장치, 소프트웨어 구성요소 간 통신과 작동을 지원하는 로봇 개발 플랫폼이다.

참가팀은 주어진 코스에서 차량이 차선을 유지하고 장애물을 피하며 목적지까지 안정적으로 주행하도록 알고리즘을 구현했다. 심사에서는 코스 이탈과 장애물 충돌 횟수, 완주 시간 등을 종합적으로 평가했다. 그 결과 딥러닝 기반 자율주행 차량 부문에서는 인천 삼산고등학교가, ROS2 기반 피지컬 AI 차량 부문에서는 인천 송도고등학교가 각각 우승했다.

현대모비스가 2018년부터 운영해 온 자율주행차 경진대회는 학생들이 소프트웨어 알고리즘을 실제 차량 제어에 적용하는 경험을 제공하는 프로그램이다. 올해는 참가 학생들을 대상으로 소프트웨어 사전 교육도 지원했다.

공학 토론 대회에서는 현대모비스가 개발한 정규 교과목 ‘공학 커뮤니케이션’을 이수한 학생들이 공학과 기술 분야의 주요 현안을 놓고 토론했다. 학생들은 기술적 근거를 바탕으로 상대 주장을 분석하고 자신의 의견을 논리적으로 전달하는 역량을 겨뤘다.

함께 열린 청년공학 학술대회에서는 AI와 자율주행, 센서 기술, 최적화 알고리즘 등을 주제로 학생들이 수행한 연구 결과가 발표됐다. 특히 올해는 기술 개발뿐 아니라 미래 모빌리티가 사회에 미치는 영향을 인문사회적 관점에서 분석한 연구도 소개됐다.

현대모비스는 이러한 활동을 일회성 체험 행사에 그치지 않고 학교 정규 교육과정과 연결하고 있다. 회사는 2024년 자동차 부품업계 최초로 고교학점제와 연계한 정규 교과목 교재 ‘공학 커뮤니케이션’을 발간했으며, 2025년에는 ‘인공지능 자율주행 자동차 탐구’ 교육과정을 추가로 선보였다.

두 교육과정은 교육감 승인을 받은 과목으로 운영되고 있으며, 현재 전국 14개 일반계 고등학교에서 약 1,800명의 학생이 자율주행과 로보틱스 등 미래 모빌리티 분야의 기초 지식을 배우고 있다. 학생들은 정규 수업을 통해 공학적 사고와 기술 이해 능력을 쌓고, 경진대회와 연구 발표를 통해 학습 내용을 실제 문제 해결에 적용하는 경험을 얻는다.

한성희 현대모비스 지속가능경영실장은 “청소년 공학 리더 프로그램은 학생들이 학교에서 배운 공학 지식을 바탕으로 문제 해결 역량을 기르고 자발적인 연구활동으로 확장할 수 있도록 지원하는 프로그램”이라며 “미래 모빌리티 산업을 이끌 창의적 공학 인재 양성을 위해 지원을 지속 확대해 나갈 계획”이라고 밝혔다.

이번 행사는 AI와 로보틱스 기술을 고등학교 정규 교육과정에 접목하고, 학생들이 직접 알고리즘을 개발해 실제 주행 환경에서 검증하도록 했다는 점에서 의미가 있다. 특히 자율주행차 경진대회와 공학 토론, 학술 연구를 연계한 교육 방식은 소프트웨어 개발 능력뿐 아니라 기술적 판단과 협업, 문제 해결 역량을 함께 기르는 데 초점을 맞추고 있다.

한편, 현대모비스는 앞으로도 학교 교육과 실습 중심 프로그램을 연계해 미래 모빌리티 분야의 공학 인재 육성을 확대할 계획이다.
articles.summary: 현대모비스는 전국 12개 고등학교 학생 약 100명이 참가한 청소년 공학 리더 페스티벌에서 딥러닝 자율주행 차량과 ROS2 기반 피지컬 AI 차량 경진대회를 운영했다. 학생들은 차선·교통신호 인식과 장애물 회피 알고리즘을 모형 자동차에 적용했으며, 코스 이탈·충돌 횟수와 완주 시간 등을 기준으로 평가받았다. 특히 ROS2 부문은 센서, 제어 장치, 소프트웨어 구성요소를 연결하는 로봇 개발 플랫폼을 실제 주행 과제에 활용하도록 했다는 점에서 교육적 의미가 있다. 관련 정규 교육과정은 전국 14개 일반계 고등학교의 약 1,800명에게 제공되고 있어, 이번 행사는 새로운 상용 기술 발표보다는 국내 자율주행·로보틱스 인재 기반 확대 사례로 볼 수 있다.
